title: Computer Science Fundamentals for Working Professionals
summary: Master the core pillars of computer science—data structures, algorithms, system design basics, and core architecture—to build efficient, scalable software.

days.title: How Computers Store Data: Memory and Variables
objectives: Explain how RAM stores variables using memory addresses
Differentiate between stack and heap memory allocation

days.title: Arrays and Strings in Memory
objectives: Calculate memory offsets for contiguous array elements
Identify performance bottlenecks of string manipulation

days.title: Linked Lists: Pointers and Nodes
objectives: Draw node references for singly and doubly linked lists
Compare time complexities of insertions in arrays versus linked lists

days.title: Stacks and Queues: LIFO and FIFO
objectives: Implement a stack using basic array operations
Explain real-world queue use cases like task scheduling

days.title: Hash Maps and Collision Resolution
objectives: Explain how hash functions map keys to indices
Resolve collisions using chaining and open addressing

days.title: Introduction to Big O Notation
objectives: Calculate time complexity for simple loops
Differentiate between O(1), O(n), and O(n^2) runtimes

days.title: Searching Algorithms: Linear and Binary Search
objectives: Implement binary search on a sorted dataset
Determine when to apply binary search over linear search

days.title: Basic Sorting: Bubble, Selection, and Insertion Sort
objectives: Trace the state of an array through insertion sort passes
Compare worst-case efficiencies of basic sorting algorithms

days.title: Efficient Sorting: Merge Sort and Quick Sort
objectives: Explain the divide-and-conquer strategy in merge sort
Choose appropriate sorting algorithms based on dataset constraints

days.title: Recursion Fundamentals
objectives: Identify the base case and recursive step in a function
Trace call stack growth during recursive execution

days.title: Relational Databases & Normalization
objectives: Design normalized tables up to 3rd Normal Form
Define primary and foreign keys to enforce relationships

days.title: SQL Query Optimization & Indexes
objectives: Write efficient JOIN queries across multiple tables
Explain how B-Trees improve database lookup speeds

days.title: Transactions and ACID Properties
objectives: Explain each letter of the ACID acronym with examples
Identify scenarios requiring database transaction rollbacks

days.title: NoSQL Concepts and Choosing a Database
objectives: Compare document-oriented storage with relational schemas
Select between SQL and NoSQL based on application requirements

days.title: Caching Strategies
objectives: Design cache-aside patterns using Redis or Memcached
Define cache invalidation strategies for frequently updated data

days.title: How the Web Works: HTTP and DNS
objectives: Trace the DNS lookup process when a URL is entered
Analyze HTTP request and response status codes

days.title: API Design and REST Principles
objectives: Design clean RESTful endpoints using proper HTTP verbs
Structure JSON request and response payloads effectively

days.title: Concurrency, Threads, and Processes
objectives: Differentiate between operating system processes and threads
Identify race conditions in multithreaded environments

days.title: Basic Cybersecurity and Authentication
objectives: Explain token-based authentication using JWT
Prevent common vulnerabilities like SQL injection and XSS

days.title: System Scalability and Load Balancing
objectives: Explain horizontal versus vertical scaling strategies
Describe how load balancers distribute traffic across servers
